title: Integer isosceles triangles
statement: How many non-congruent isosceles triangles with positive integer side lengths have perimeter 29?
hint: Write the sides as a,a,b with 2a+b=29; triangle inequality is the real filter.

title: A diagonal must satisfy two triangle inequalities
statement: A quadrilateral has side lengths 8, 15, 20 and 27, in some order. A proposed diagonal has length among 10, 12, 18, 22, 30, 35. Find the sum of those proposed lengths that can occur as a diagonal for at least one ordering of the four sides.
hint: A diagonal must form two valid triangles at the same time.

title: Cylinder mensuration with an integer filter
statement: A closed right circular cylinder has positive integer radius r and height h. Its total surface area is numerically equal to twice its volume. If its volume is kπ, find the least possible value of k.
hint: Cancel the common 2πr factor before using the integer condition.

title: Regular-polygon angle arithmetic
statement: For how many integers m with 3 ≤ m ≤ 30 is the interior angle of a regular m-gon an even integer number of degrees?
hint: Rewrite the interior angle as 180° - 360°/m and test divisibility.

title: Cube distance interpretation
statement: Two vertices of a cube are (1,1,1) and (3,5,1). Depending on their positions in the cube, the segment joining them may be an edge, a face diagonal or a body diagonal. Find the least possible surface area of such a cube.
hint: The given distance is √20. Decide which cube distance type makes the side length smallest.

title: Square, trisection points and crossing lines
statement: In square ABCD of side 12, points E,F trisect CD, with CE=EF=FD. Lines AE and BF meet at M. Find the area of △MAB.
hint: Coordinates make the two crossing lines linear; place the square on the axes.

title: Centroid and midpoint area
statement: In triangle ABC, E and F are the midpoints of AC and AB, respectively. Medians BE and CF meet at centroid G. Let Y,Z be the midpoints of BE,CF. If [ABC]=720, find [GYZ].
hint: Use centroid and midpoint ratios to express G,Y,Z affinely; area scales from the original triangle.

title: An acute-triangle threshold
statement: Let X={n,n+2,n+4,…,n+20}. Find the smallest positive integer n such that any three numbers chosen from X, not necessarily distinct, can be the side lengths of an acute triangle.
hint: Test the worst triple: make the largest side as large as possible and the other two as small as allowed.

title: Altitude to the hypotenuse
statement: A right triangle has altitude 6 to its hypotenuse. What is the least possible length of the hypotenuse?
hint: Use h²=pq with p+q=c, then maximize pq for fixed c.

title: A divided side in a right triangle
statement: In right triangle ABC, ∠B=90°. Point D lies on BC and BD:DC=3:1, AB+BD=AC+CD. If AC:AB=p:q in lowest terms, find p+q.
hint: Let DC=t, so BD=3t and BC=4t; translate the length equation before Pythagoras.

title: Two circles tangent internally to a larger circle
statement: A circle S has radius 12 and centre O. Circles S1,S2 touch S internally and intersect at distinct points A,B. If ∠OAB=90°, find the sum of the radii of S1,S2.
hint: The common chord AB is perpendicular to the line joining the small-circle centres; use the right angle at A to locate O relative to that structure.

title: A parallel chord through a midpoint
statement: In isosceles triangle ABC, AB=AC=12, BC=18. Let D be the foot of the altitude from A to BC, and let M be the midpoint of AD. The line through M parallel to BC cuts the circumcircle of ABC in P,Q. Find PQ.
hint: Use symmetry to put the circumcenter and chord PQ on the altitude line, then use half-chord geometry.

title: Ptolemy in a cyclic rectangle
statement: A rectangle ABCD has side lengths 5 and 12 and is inscribed in a circle. Find the length of diagonal BD.
hint: A rectangle is cyclic, and both diagonals are equal.

title: Tangent-secant power
statement: From a point P outside a circle, PT is tangent with PT=12. A secant from P meets the circle first at A and then at B, with PA=8. Find PB.
hint: Use the whole secant distance in PT²=PA·PB.

title: Ceva’s theorem
statement: In triangle ABC, points D∈BC, E∈CA, F∈AB satisfy BD:DC=2:3, CE:EA=4:5. If AD,BE,CF are concurrent and AF:FB=p:q in lowest terms, find p+q.
hint: Write the three Ceva ratios in cyclic order and solve only for the missing one.

title: Menelaus’ theorem
statement: In triangle ABC, D∈BC, E∈CA, while F lies on the extension of AB. Suppose D,E,F are collinear and BD:DC=2:1, CE:EA=3:2. If |AF:FB|=p:q in lowest terms, find p+q.
hint: The extension point makes the directed third ratio negative; take the absolute value only at the end.

title: Sine rule
statement: In triangle ABC, A=30°, B=45°, a=BC=6. If b=CA, find b².
hint: Match each side with its opposite angle before using the sine rule.

title: Coordinate circle
statement: The line y=3 cuts the circle x²+y²=25 at points P,Q. Find PQ.
hint: Substitute y=3 into the circle equation; the two x-values are symmetric.

title: Vector parallelogram
statement: Points A=(1,2), B=(4,7), C=(10,8) are three consecutive vertices of parallelogram ABCD. If D=(u,v), find u+v.
hint: For consecutive vertices A,B,C,D use D=A+C-B.

title: Locus of points equidistant from two lines
statement: The line y=2 meets the locus of points equidistant from the coordinate axes at two points P,Q. Find PQ.
hint: Equidistant from the coordinate axes means y=x or y=-x.
